title: Ideal coefficient estimate under reindexing
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^{[n]}\to\{-1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq[n]$, and fix a sign assignment $z:P\to\{-1,1\}$. Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\delta\leq1/2$, and take a batch of free-coordinate sign assignments indexed by the restricted sample count for $(P,k,\delta)$. For any frequency $S$ in the family of subsets of the free coordinates of size at most $\lfloor3k/4\rfloor$, the real value of the empirical rational Fourier coefficient computed from the batch labeled by the restriction of $f$ at $z$ equals the empirical real Fourier coefficient of the reindexed restricted function, computed on the corresponding reindexed inputs.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
the input batch is indexed by the restricted sample count
$S$ belongs to the low-degree family on the free coordinates
